extracted.intended_audience: general readers and practitioners of improvisational theatre / performance (people seeking information about Theatresports and related competitive improv formats)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Theatresports form of competitive improvisational theatre — its defining features, how performances are generated, and how winners are determined, including notable derivatives and variations. Useful for performers, producers, and researchers interested in competitive improv formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a competition format for dramatic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatresports is a form of improvisational theatre, which uses the format of a competition for dramatic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competitive framing itself is a defining quality — structuring performances as contests between opposing teams to increase tension and audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposing teams perform scenes based on audience suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposing teams can perform scenes based on audience suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scene prompts are drawn from the audience; teams must improvise material in response to those suggestions, which shapes the spontaneity and challenge of performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating and judging (audience or panel) determines winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Performances are rated by the audience or by a panel of judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation can be democratic (audience voting) or adjudicated (judges), and these ratings are used to decide outcomes — making clarity about who rates and how an important procedural criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on sports-like competition mechanics (e.g., referee, points, fouls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivatives such as ComedySportz tend to emphasise the sports competition format more than Theatresports, for example by having a referee who awards points and administers fouls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extent to which a show adopts overt 'sports' mechanics (referees, point-scoring, fouls) is an axis of variation and an evaluative/design choice that affects tone, pacing, and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of techniques to generate audience reaction ('heat')
rubrics_metrics.description: The concept of Theatresports originated in Johnstone's observations of techniques used in professional wrestling to generate heat, or audience reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate dramaturgical techniques aimed at provoking audience response (conflict, rivalry, callbacks) are part of the format's purpose and should be considered when designing or evaluating a show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability to different media and derivative formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows and companies (e.g., ComedySportz, Thank God You're Here, TheatreGames LIVE, Face Off Unlimited, Ligue nationale d'improvisation, Canadian Improv Games) have adapted the concept to various productions and formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion for Theatresports-style formats is how well the competitive improvisation structure can be adapted for different venues (live stage, television) and institutional contexts; variations may change emphasis (sportification, televised structure) while retaining core elements.
